fields.narrative_intro: *A bewildered person and a disheveled person discuss Figma's MCP whitelist excluding Pi inside a 404 error page on a site that no longer exists.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
BEWILDERED PERSON: "Figma restricted MCP access to whitelisted clients."
DISHEVELED PERSON: "Pi was excluded."
fields.panel2:
[build]
BEWILDERED PERSON: "Is Pi unavailable?"
DISHEVELED PERSON: "No. Merely unauthorized."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
BEWILDERED PERSON: "So Pi is a 403, not a 404."
DISHEVELED PERSON: "It was found, then excluded."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The 404 page quietly changes its number to 403; a tiny Pi-shaped dot remains outside a velvet rope.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
DISHEVELED PERSON: "Pi was not missing. It was administratively absent."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The site disappears, leaving its 403 sign beside a completely blank whitelist.]

narrative_summary: Figma's exclusion of Pi gets reclassified from a 404 into the more bureaucratic 403.
rationale: Candidate 1 turns the exact 404-versus-403 distinction into a sharp bureaucratic status joke, with “administratively absent” functioning as an earned punchline rather than a restatement. The other pitches mostly replay the obvious 404/access-denied premise without matching that level of conceptual precision.
story_title: Figma restricts MCP access to whitelisted clients, excluding Pi
place: inside a 404 error page on a site that no longer exists
hat_pair: foam stock chart spiking upward worn as a pointed hat with a tiny flag at the peak
shower cap covered in sticky notes
